desc:
Spreadsheet columns are labelled A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ..., AZ, BA, ..., ZZ, AAA, ... Given the label title of a column, return its 1-based position.

"A"  -> 1
"Z"  -> 26
"AA" -> 27
"AZ" -> 52
"ZY" -> 701
constraints: title consists of uppercase English letters only
The column number is at most 2<sup>31</sup> - 1 (the largest valid title is "FXSHRXW")
hints: Look at "AB": it is like a two-digit number, but the digits are letters.
This is a base-26 number system where the digits run from 1 (A) to 26 (Z) instead of 0 to 25.
Scan left to right keeping result; for each letter do result = result * 26 + (letter - 'A' + 1).
editorial: Treat the label as a number in base 26 whose digits are A=1, ..., Z=26. There is no zero digit, which is why the system is called bijective base 26. Reading from the most significant letter, the usual positional rule applies: multiply what you have by 26 and add the value of the next letter.
For example "ZY" = 26 * 26 + 25 = 701. The loop touches each letter once, so the work is proportional to the label length, and the result stays within 32 bits by the constraint.
